title: Logistics Event (fact_event)
description: One Layer 2 operational event, Layer 3 external driver, or Layer 4 discovery lead. The three classes are separated at the contract level: an external driver cannot be presented as a logistics impact unless its transmission chain is complete, and a discovery lead can never be the sole evidence for a material impact conclusion. Mode-neutral -- 'modes' carries the affected transport modes, so the same contract serves Air and Land events later.

event_class.description: Layer separation per scope document Sections 3.4 and 6. 'direct_operational_event' is a Logistics operational event; 'external_driver' is contextual until a transmission mechanism is stated; 'discovery_lead' is an unconfirmed lead.

lifecycle_status.description: Evidence lifecycle per WO-010 Gate G. 'insufficient_evidence' and 'closed' are legitimate terminal answers, not failures.

lane_relevance.description: Per-lane relevance. An empty list is valid and means no lane relevance has been established -- which is different from, and must not be displayed as, no relevance existing.

thailand_relevance_basis.description: Why the event is (or is not) Thailand-relevant. Required to be non-empty whenever thailand_relevance is not 'none_established'.

conflicting_evidence.description: Explicitly preserved conflicts. Where sources disagree both positions are kept; the platform does not silently select a preferred answer.

resolution_status.description: WO-049 (Issue #92) item 6: two additive values (escalated_for_verification, resolved_as_status_change), matching the precedent of WO-035's additive enum extension and WO-047's own impact_assessment.status +2. The original four values are unchanged.

contradiction_type.description: WO-049 (Issue #92) item 6, additive. Only 'existence' and 'status_change' cap the Development-level evidence_grade and force situation_state UNCERTAIN (analysis/grading.py); the other six are recorded and displayed without degrading the assessment. Optional and nullable so every one of the 10 committed events (conflicting_evidence: []) stays valid unchanged.

claim_ids_side_a.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. The claims on one side of the disagreement -- never a merged sentence.

claim_ids_side_b.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. The claims on the other side.

independence_groups_a.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. Derived from claim_ids_side_a's documents; lets a card say '3 origins vs 1 origin' rather than 'sources disagree'.

independence_groups_b.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. Derived from claim_ids_side_b's documents.

first_detected_at.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. When the disagreement was first recorded.

last_reviewed_at.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. The re-verification SLA clock.

resolution_basis.description: WO-049 item 6, additive. Required (non-empty) whenever resolution_status is not 'unresolved' -- no contradiction may leave 'unresolved' without a stated reason, and no contradiction may be resolved without one either. Checked in scripts/validate.py, not this schema, since it is a conditional-on-value rule this schema already expresses the same way document.schema.json's rights.reviewer_record does.

transmission_chain.description: External driver -> operational change -> Logistics mechanism -> observable indicator -> observed impact / potential impact / scenario. Every link is nullable, and completeness is computed from which links are present; a chain with a missing link makes the item contextual or an unresolved hypothesis, never a conclusion.

impact_assessments.description: The nine impact areas, each assessed independently. Event severity, logistics impact severity, evidence strength and confidence are separate fields and none may be inferred from another.

event_severity.description: Severity of the event itself, kept deliberately separate from every impact_assessments[].severity. These must never be inferred from one another.

negative_operational_evidence.description: True only when an actual assessment found negative operational evidence. Required to be true before any impact area may use status 'no_material'.

closure_basis.description: Why the event was closed. Required to be non-null when lifecycle_status is 'closed'.

clustering.description: Deterministic minimum clustering inputs (WO-010 Gate G). Unrelated events must not merge merely because they concern the same country or conflict.

merge_status.description: WO-049 (Issue #92) item 11: standardised on collectors/event_identity.py::MERGE_STATUSES' vocabulary (matched_external_id / matched_fingerprint), not the matched_source_record / matched_cluster_key values this field previously declared. That original vocabulary was never referenced by any code path or committed record; event_identity.py's vocabulary is the one actually used by resolve_event_identity, candidate_event.schema.json, reviewed_event.schema.json and data/reviewed/current_events.json, so it is the load-bearing one. The four other values are unchanged. matched_external_id now also covers the claim-attachment rule 2 case (design part 1 Section 1.4: an exact official-identifier or attribution-chain match); matched_fingerprint covers rule 3 (the deterministic type/date/geography/entity gate).

active_as_of.description: The instant at which this event was last confirmed still active, from retrieved or human-reviewed evidence. Null means activity has not been confirmed; an event with a null event_end_date is NOT active by default.

active_basis.description: What establishes that the event was still active at active_as_of. Required alongside active_as_of; an assertion of activity with no basis is not publishable.

situation_state.description: WO-047 (Issue #89) / Issue #88 comment 2 Section 7.3. Additive, optional and nullable so every existing committed record remains valid unchanged. Orthogonal to lifecycle_status: lifecycle_status answers 'how well do we know this?', situation_state answers 'what is the situation doing?'. Not authored directly by AI for RESOLVED (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 7.4); scripts/validate.py enforces the L3 firewall and the RESOLVED gating rule.

claim_ids.description: WO-047. Optional; absent or empty means no Claim has been attached to this event yet. The Claim x Document -> event_evidence adapter (analysis/claim_evidence_adapter.py) is what actually populates evidence_ids from these.

evidence_grade.description: WO-047. The four user-facing evidence-grade categories (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 8), computed from the claim set -- never authored directly. Optional and nullable; distinct from the existing item-level evidence.strength A-D, which is unchanged.

superseded_by.description: WO-047. The forward counterpart to the existing supersedes array, needed for a clean merge: the absorbed event points forward to the event it was merged into.

verified_facts.description: WO-047. Derived partition of claim_ids by claim_type; never authored directly. One of the four claim-partition arrays that keep facts, reports and inference physically separate (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 7.2).

grade_override.description: WO-049 (Issue #92) item 3: a downgrade-only override of the computed evidence_grade (analysis/grading.py::compute_evidence_grade). 'to' must be strictly weaker than the computed grade on the order CONFIRMED > CORROBORATED > REPORTED > ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE > null -- an upward override is not representable by this schema's enum alone and is refused by scripts/validate.py's grade_override upward-refusal rule, mirroring scripts/manual_intake.py's evidence_layer directional check. Optional and nullable so every WO-047 event stays valid unchanged.
